Earliest listed publication among matched versions, not proof of an unedited contemporaneous archive. Claim timestamps refer to the reviewed version.

## Summary

Danny Moses and Eisman examine higher rates, AI financing concentration, private-market incentives and fiscal risk. Moses favors diversified cash-generating technology on pullbacks but avoids weak neocloud balance sheets. Eisman stresses concentration and a long difficult period for leveraged PE. Both distinguish technological progress from investable returns. Moses's QE certainty and reserve concerns remain his own views, not Eisman predictions; Eisman emphasizes the lack of a comparable Treasury substitute.

Claims are assessed individually. Empirical premises are not treated as successful forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal stories remain unresolved; subjective investment judgments are not assigned directional wins.

### 015. Nvidia's reported concentration of 70% of receivables in five accounts shows major customer risk, which he then describes as 70% of revenue.

**Mixed** | Steve Eisman | material factual premise | supporting

[Source at 20:20-21:45](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bjikXzIJqSM&t=1220s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The 70% receivables concentration is confirmed, but it cannot be relabeled as 70% of revenue. NVIDIA discloses revenue concentration separately, and the downstream labs are not identified by this receivables statistic.

Qualification: The shift from accounts receivable to revenue is unsupported even if the receivables figure is correct.

Assessment test: Inspect the original 10-Q and distinguish receivables concentration, direct customers and end customers.

- [NVIDIA Q2 FY2027 Form 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000075/nvda-20260726.htm) (2026-08-27): Five customers represented 22%,14%,13%,11%,10% of receivables. This is not the revenue-concentration statistic; direct and indirect customer exposures are distinct.

## Framework and tools

- Compare financing structures and incentives across cycles.
- Separate core franchise cash flow from marginal speculative capex.
- Treat concentration and maturity mismatch as distinct risks.
- Recognize short-selling timing and carry constraints.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- CoreWeave debt including leases
- Nvidia receivable concentration
- 2000 telecom vendor financing
- Mortgage warehouse-line resale economics
- PE gates and mark-to-model
- Reserve shares and household wealth

## Source cautions

Danny Moses supplies most cycle, private-credit and gold/QE claims. Eisman is separated where he adds the higher-for-longer, housing and concentration arguments.
- A third-party strategist's S&P target is transcribed ambiguously as 6800 or 7800 and his rate forecast is repeatedly corrected; it is not treated as an Eisman prediction.
- Nvidia receivables are subsequently described as revenue without substantiation.
